Files to take apart

Drop video files or folders here Folders are searched completely.

What this does

Takes each file in the queue apart: a silent picture file plus every audio track and every subtitle as its own file, written next to the source. Your source file stays where it is and is not touched.

The details
  • Every track is copied exactly as it is: audio keeps its own format (.ac3, .dts, .eac3, .m4a, .flac …), subtitles stay untouched.
  • The silent picture keeps the source container — an MP4 stays an MP4, everything else becomes MKV.
  • Files with more than one track open a chooser, so you decide what gets pulled out.
  • No stereo mix here: a downmix would be a re-encode, and this route never re-encodes.
  • Nothing is cleaned up either, so Join can put it back together unchanged.
The details
  • The picture is copied, never re-encoded — it only loses its sound.
  • Audio is re-encoded to AAC wherever DaVinci would struggle: AC3, E-AC3, DTS, TrueHD, Opus, Vorbis and FLAC, anything with a layout other than mono, stereo or 5.1, and anything above 48 kHz. Everything else is copied as it is.
  • Text subtitles become cleaned-up .srt files; picture subtitles (PGS) are copied unchanged as .sup.
  • Files with more than one track open a chooser, so you decide what gets pulled out.
  • Audio with more than two channels can additionally be written as a stereo mix — it is in the chooser as its own line, and “keep all” does not include it.
There are no other options here — what the Convert page is set to makes no difference to either route.

Files to join

Drop the video file plus its audio and subtitle files here They are sorted by extension. Dropping a folder adds the files inside it.

What this does

Builds one new MKV out of separate parts: a video file plus the audio and subtitle files you drop next to it.

The details
  • The audio files you add replace the sound of the video file. Add subtitles only, and the video keeps its own sound.
  • Subtitles already inside the video file are never carried over — add them as files.
  • Your files stay where they are; the result is always a new file next to the video file.
  • One job per run: exactly one video file, plus at least one audio or subtitle file.
  • A .sub only works together with its .idx of the same name — drop both.
  • The converter names the result itself: it tidies the base name (spaces become dots) and picks another name if that one is taken.
The video can be .mkv .mp4 .m4v .mov — other formats cannot be used as a base here.

What this does

Keeps an eye on one folder and converts every video that turns up in it — on its own, without you dropping anything in.

No folder chosen yet.
What happens while this is on
  • Every video that turns up in that folder — or in any folder inside it — is converted on its own, with the options set below.
  • A file is only picked up once it has stopped growing for 30 seconds, so a download that is still running is left alone.
  • What is already in the folder when you switch on is taken along. Finished results and their sources are skipped, and so is the originals folder.
  • Watching only lasts while this window is open — closing it ends the standing order.
  • The results are written into an output folder next to their sources, and your originals are moved wherever your INI says. The watched folder will look different afterwards.
  • One video at a time here, whatever the Convert page is set to. This runs in the background, and the card still has to be free for the work you start by hand.

Options for the watched folder

No “shut down when finished” here: a standing order that switches the machine off after the first video would never convert the second one. What each setting does is explained on the Convert page — the words are the same, only the choice is separate.

Expert settings — safe to ignore, here for tinkering
Subtitle cleaner — the lines it throws away
Only when you take files apart for DaVinci. Split and Join never touch a subtitle, and an ordinary conversion does not clean either — so nothing here changes those. A phrase deletes every subtitle block it turns up in, upper or lower case makes no difference. Tick exact and a block only goes if it reads exactly like this and nothing else.
Changes apply to the next run; a run in progress keeps the settings it started with. The version before your last save is kept as NVENCForge_Config.ini.bak.
